title: PwC lifts code-generation accuracy from ~10% to 70%+ with validating agents
summary: PwC re-engineered SDLC workflows with CrewAI agents that generate, execute and iteratively validate code in a proprietary language, reading runtime logs to fix their own errors instead of one-shot generation.
agent_role: Agents generated code, ran it in real runtime environments, analyzed log output and retried; PwC engineers designed the workflow and own production deployment.
outcome: "We went from roughly 10% accuracy on code generation to 70%+ once we brought Crew AI agents into the workflow" (Jacob Wilson, PwC)
what_they_did: PwC needed faster, more accurate generation of code in a proprietary language, plus long spec documents. Its early GenAI prototypes got no real-time feedback. The team rebuilt its software workflows on CrewAI, with agents that generate code, run it and validate it in repeated passes. Agents also draft and refine functional and technical specs while consultants give feedback. CrewAI's monitoring tracked agent choices, run times and accuracy for leadership dashboards.
how_it_went: PwC's Jacob Wilson is quoted saying accuracy went from roughly 10% to 70%+ once CrewAI agents joined the workflow. The case study also says turnaround on complex documents fell, without giving a figure.
worth_knowing: This is CrewAI's own case study. PwC says per-agent visibility into task times, tool choices and human-versus-agent effort was key to proving ROI and regaining consultant trust.
prompt: Set up a CrewAI crew that writes code in [language] for [task description]. One agent writes the code. A second agent runs it in [test environment] and reads the logs and errors. If it fails, send the log analysis back to the first agent for a fix, for up to [N] attempts. Record each attempt's outcome and runtime in a summary table. Stop and show me the final code and test results. Do not deploy or merge anything without my approval.
